authority: User request on 2026-11-03: make skill discovery model aware so LeanREA loads for open-weight models and stays hidden for others, including within the same agent.
baseline: LeanREA source exists but is blocked from all shared discovery. Shared skills have no per-request model predicate.
decision: Extend native runtime hooks with a shared explicit model policy; retain universal shared exclusion.

alternatives.approach: Move a shared directory whenever a model changes
alternatives.reason: Concurrent sessions share the directory and would race; loaded history would remain exposed.

alternatives.approach: Add prose telling closed models to ignore LeanREA
alternatives.reason: Does not hide discovery or prevent the native skill reader from loading it.
A generic tool call does not supply a trustworthy active model identity or remove stale outbound history.

alternatives.approach: Native request hooks and guarded source reader
alternatives.reason: The host supplies effective request model identity and owns model changes, settings and outbound context.

omp.native: OMP automatic extension discovery + native RPC model switching + loopback transport

checks.name: Native committed text readback with real Git fixtures
Existing native configuration completion regressions
checks.result: 20 passed; stale mock source bindings were repaired after reproducing the same baseline fixture failures

checks.name: Node policy, native control and provider-format regressions
Shared fleet and LeanREA source preservation
checks.result: LeanREA package and the other 16 shared skill packages remain byte-identical to the baseline

checks.name: Native settings
checks.result: Only the new Hermes plugin was enabled; existing enabled entries including a preexisting local entry were preserved. Runtime model/provider/reasoning defaults have unchanged native readback.

limits: Codex has no documented supported live model-aware skill discovery hook, so LeanREA remains hidden there.
Known public metadata classifies exact routes; unknown aliases stay hidden until reviewed metadata is refreshed.

Managed catalog/list/view material is removed from an ineligible outbound copy. Stored history and unrelated user content are preserved. Derived reasoning and arbitrary filesystem access are outside this mechanism.
Existing processes need one reload/restart to discover the adapter. Later model switches are handled per request.
Google and Bedrock request layouts use native-source-bound shape tests; actual native loopback transport execution covers OpenAI-compatible requests.
Native Python middleware was exercised with the installed dependency-ready Python 3.11 environment. No real model inference or comparative model-quality trial was performed.
Publication and final installed loading require the separate canonical deployment receipt.

change_reconciliation.requirement_reason: The user extended universal exclusion into per-model discovery and automatic on-demand loading within a native agent.
change_reconciliation.authority: Explicit user request quoted in this record; narrow LeanREA scope and existing native permissions remain binding.
change_reconciliation.checks: 11 Python discovery tests, 7 Node tests, 6 real-Git native text tests, 20 configuration completion tests, 8 retirement tests; native Hermes middleware and OMP automatic extension discovery/model-switch/loopback settings probes.

outcome_review.expected: Known open-weight requests discover and can load LeanREA; closed/unknown requests do not, including after switching within the same agent.
outcome_review.observed: Native closed/open/closed transitions pass, native settings remain effective, generated restricted history is removed from disallowed outbound copies, and unrelated skill packages/defaults are preserved.
outcome_review.evidence: The source bindings, native transition results, settings cases and targeted check counts in this record.
outcome_review.limitations: No Codex dynamic hook, remote model attestation, filesystem sandboxing, removal of previously derived reasoning, real inference or model-quality claim. Publication and loaded-state readback are separate.
